steps: 1. Take company name + any domain from the posting (apply URL host, ATS board token, company email domain).
2. Normalise name (strip legal suffixes: Ltd, GmbH, Inc, BV, Pte Ltd, LLC, AG, SA, Pvt).
3. If an ATS board (Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby etc.) lists a company website, use that as the canonical domain.
4. Query Wikidata wbsearchentities; accept a candidate only if its P856 website host matches the domain (or the country matches and the label is an exact normalised match).
5. Country registry: GB -> Companies House; US -> SEC EDGAR (listed only); elsewhere -> GLEIF fuzzy search.
6. Match against destination sponsor register (see countries/<iso2>.json) using normalised name; record match quality (exact/fuzzy).
7. Store resolution confidence; if nothing resolves, mark company as 'unverified' (scam signal vague_company).

scam_signals.description: Candidate asked to pay for the job: registration, processing, training, visa, 'security deposit', certification, equipment.
scam_signals.detect: Regex on posting/description/message text: (registration|processing|visa|placement|training|security|refundable) (fee|charge|deposit), 'pay .* (INR|Rs|₹|USD|\$)', 'advance payment'. FTC: honest employers never ask you to pay to get a job. MEA: overcharging Rs 2-5 lakh reported; legal RA service charge capped at Rs 30,000 + 18% GST (ECR recruitment only).

scam_signals.description: Offer of a work visa / 'guaranteed visa' or sponsorship in exchange for money.
scam_signals.detect: Text match: 'guaranteed visa', 'visa guarantee', '100% visa', 'work permit .* fee', 'sponsorship .* (fee|cost) .* candidate'. Exclude legit employer-pays statements ('we cover visa costs').

scam_signals.description: Told to travel on a tourist/visit visa and 'convert' to work visa on arrival.
scam_signals.detect: Text match: '(tourist|visit|visitor) visa' near '(convert|change|then|work permit)'. MEA: genuine offers come with an employment/work visa and a signed contract, not a tourist visa.

scam_signals.description: Lure matching the SE Asia cyber-scam compound pattern: 'Digital Sales and Marketing Executive', 'Customer Support', 'data entry' jobs in Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar or via Thailand, high pay, low requirements, recruited via social media.
scam_signals.detect: Job location in KH/LA/MM (or TH with onward travel / border cities e.g. Mae Sot, Golden Triangle SEZ) AND role keywords (digital marketing, customer support, data entry, crypto, chat operator, 'typing job') AND (salary_above_market OR messaging_only_contact). Govt: 6,998 Indians rescued from Cambodia/Myanmar/Laos centres 2022-2025.

scam_signals.description: Deposit-a-check-and-send-back, reshipping packages, or buying equipment from a 'vendor' before starting.
scam_signals.detect: Text match: '(deposit|cash) .* check', 'reship', 'receive packages', 'purchase equipment from our vendor'.

scam_signals.description: Only contact is WhatsApp/Telegram/Signal number or social DM; no company email/ATS.
scam_signals.detect: Posting has wa.me / t.me / 'WhatsApp' / 'Telegram' / phone-number-only contact and no ATS or company-domain apply link. MEA: illegal agents usually communicate only through WhatsApp.

scam_signals.description: Indian recruiting agent involved but no valid eMigrate RA licence (or appears on notified illegal agents list).
scam_signals.detect: If posting names an Indian agency/RC number, check against eMigrate 'List of active RA' and notified illegal agents (3,505 notified as of 2026-04-09). Manual/link check in v1 unless a downloadable list is confirmed.

scam_signals.description: Recruiter/apply email on a free webmail domain (gmail, yahoo, outlook, hotmail, proton, rediffmail, etc.) for a company that should have its own domain.
scam_signals.detect: Extract emails; flag if domain in free-mail list and company resolved to a corporate domain (or failed to resolve).

scam_signals.description: Pay far above market for the role/country with little required work or experience.
scam_signals.detect: Parsed salary > 1.5x the country file's salary.senior_swe_annual_gross.high (threshold is a heuristic; tune) OR phrases like 'earn .* per week from home', 'no experience required' with high pay. FTC: lots of money for little work is almost certainly a scam.

scam_signals.description: Apply URL / email domain does not match the company's resolved domain (lookalike domains, URL shorteners, form builders).
scam_signals.detect: Compare apply host and email domain with resolved company domain and known ATS hosts (greenhouse.io, lever.co, ashbyhq.com, workable.com, smartrecruiters.com, myworkdayjobs.com, etc.); flag bit.ly/forms.gle/typeform or edit-distance <=2 lookalikes.

scam_signals.description: Company cannot be resolved to any website, registry entry, or ATS board; generic name ('Global Solutions LLC'), no address.
scam_signals.detect: Entity resolution failed in all of Wikidata, national registry, GLEIF, ATS; or posting lacks company name ('confidential client') AND is not from a known recruiter.

scam_signals.description: Offer without interview, or 'selected' message before applying.
scam_signals.detect: Text: 'you have been selected', 'no interview', 'direct joining', 'offer letter within 24 hours'.

scam_signals.description: Asks for passport scan, Aadhaar/PAN, bank details before a formal offer.
scam_signals.detect: Text: '(send|share|upload) .* (passport|aadhaar|pan card|bank details|OTP)' in posting body.

scam_signals.description: Artificial urgency ('urgent hiring', 'limited seats', 'join within 3 days', 'immediate visa').
scam_signals.detect: Keyword list; low weight because many real postings say 'urgent'.

confidence_model.status: proposal - heuristic weights, tune with labelled data
confidence_model.formula: score = round( sum(w_i * f_i) / sum(w_i for available factors) * 100 ) + sum(scam penalties); clamp 0..100. If any hard_flag scam signal fires, cap at 10. If posting explicitly says no sponsorship, cap at 5. Show 'coverage' = share of weight with data so the meter can render uncertainty.

factors.justification: The app's core promise is visa-sponsored jobs; this is the factor that most often makes a lead useless for an Indian applicant, so it carries the most weight. Explicit text beats a register match because register presence only proves the employer can sponsor, not that this role will.

A sponsorship move is costly and hard to undo for the user; established, active, non-shrinking employers are less likely to withdraw offers or fail before the visa lands. Early-stage startups get partial credit, not zero, since many genuinely sponsor.

Captures degree recognition (e.g. 3-year degrees), lotteries/quotas, processing time and ECR/attestation burden; differs strongly by destination and directly affects whether an offer converts into a move.
User asked for recent jobs; stale postings are often filled and re-posted aggregator copies are a scam vector.

factors.mapping: rating/5 scaled, multiplied by volume factor min(1, log10(n_reviews)/3); unknown -> factor excluded (weight renormalised)
factors.justification: Useful but mostly link-only for a logged-out free app, so often missing; kept below sponsorship and company data. In v1 this will usually be excluded and coverage shown as reduced.

confidence_model.penalties: See scam_signals[].weight (negative points applied after weighted score).
confidence_model.display: 0-39 low (red), 40-69 medium (amber), 70-100 high (green); always show top 3 reasons and the coverage percentage.
